program: Violence interruption, trauma support and paid workforce preparation

what: Institute for Nonviolence Chicago supports people at high risk of violence in Austin, West Garfield Park and Back of the Yards.
Outreach staff mediate conflicts, support victims and connect participants with trauma-informed care.
Paid workforce preparation combines job readiness, mentorship and nonviolence training.
strengths: Local outreach can reach people underserved by conventional services.
Trauma support and job preparation address connected barriers to safety and stability.
Paid participation may make sustained attendance more feasible.
reservations: Service counts and neighborhood trends do not establish additional shootings prevented.
Evidence from longer, different interventions does not identify this recipient's clinical effect.
Government replacement, attendance burdens and transfer-payer costs materially affect donor value.

sections.what: Institute for Nonviolence Chicago, EIN 81-1098722, is the independent donation recipient. Current services include violence interruption, victim support, reentry, behavioral supports and paid workforce preparation. Official program locations establish Chicago delivery rather than relying on headquarters alone. [Programs](https://www.nonviolencechicago.org/pathwaystopeace)
sections.monitoring: The 2025 aggregate of 1,307 unique participants spans service types; it is not a workforce cohort. The reported 197 mediations and 25% neighborhood decline do not measure counterfactual violence reduction. Pathways describes twelve weeks, weekly stipends and ten in-person hours Monday through Thursday plus remote Friday work. Its 4,070 participants since 2016 are cumulative. Track distinct participants, attendance, exposure-adjusted injuries, validated trauma measures, collected net earnings and services available without the Institute.
sections.qualitative: The READI lottery evaluated an eighteen-month subsidized job and cognitive behavioral intervention, not this twelve-week program. Its primary composite violence result was not significant. Shooting victimization was 18% lower but statistically uncertain; a larger arrest reduction did not survive adjustment for multiple outcomes. Neither arrests nor neighborhood trends become QALYs here. Injury risk, causal reduction and trauma utility are explicit weak priors. Physical injury and trauma cohorts are partitioned to avoid stacking both benefits for one person. No ordinary survivor earnings are credited.
sections.cost:
FY2025 original recognized expense is $15,749,475. No direct event or rental expense group was identified in the reviewed return. The annual whole-recipient denominator prices a limited conditional channel, not the complete portfolio or a verified marginal expansion. The .5 response prior represents annual work additional to continuing public and nonprofit alternatives; b=1 is reported separately, not another donation haircut on realized outcomes.

A judged 500 local household opportunities yield 250 additional exposed households and 125 clinical participants. A .05 injury risk and .1 causal reduction imply .625 avoided victimizations. One integrated physical QALY per event is truncated within three years, excludes trauma and is not repeated annually. The other 124.375 people receive .03 utility for half a year. Retaining .8 of positive health components and applying a one-year delay at 3% gives 1.934466 clinical QALYs.

Resource exposure is independent of clinical success. One participant household carries one modeled welfareperson; other family welfare is unpriced. For 62.5 households, judged net job resources of $1,500 and net stipends of $300 each retain .5 of positive components, while the full $300 attendance burden remains: $600 net. The other 187.5 households net −$150. Negative job changes and stipends retain their full sign separately before household netting and a single log. At $15,000 annual household resources for one finite year, .5 × [62.5 log(1.04) + 187.5 log(.99)] / 1.03 = .275173 equivalent healthy years. Combined 2.209639 yields $71.276232 million per ten combined equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs.

Job resources are after taxes, benefit withdrawal, replacement earnings and new-job commuting or care costs. Stipends are after taxes and benefits; attendance costs separately cover class time, early foregone work and travel. All dollar amounts are hypotheses, not observed collected gains. Costs remain when clinical effects fail. Central payer and outside care costs are unknown-neutral references, not factual zeros. Matched stipend losses and external care burdens are explicit stresses. Government opportunity costs, nonlocal incidence, displacement and full portfolio effects remain unknown.
sections.funding: FY2025 government grants are $13,950,007 and grants to domestic individuals $942,369; neither establishes net new household income. Annual recognized expenses for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 are $10,268,003, $12,274,566 and $15,749,475, mean $12,764,014.67. Funding replacement and a specific unfunded donor expansion were not established. A secondary index flags a possible FY2025 control finding; the original audit was not verified in this bounded phase, so this is a follow-up lead rather than a factual audit conclusion.

model.costScope: FY2025 original recognized expense is $15,749,475. No direct event or rental expense group was identified in the reviewed return. The annual whole-recipient denominator prices a limited conditional channel, not the complete portfolio or a verified marginal expansion. The .5 response prior represents annual work additional to continuing public and nonprofit alternatives; b=1 is reported separately, not another donation haircut on realized outcomes.
model.geographicAttribution: Chicago neighborhoods; all modeled participants local, not a national result.
model.formula: Q = positiveOnly(events × integrated injury Q, .8) + positiveOnly((treated − events) × trauma utility × .5 years, .8), discounted one year. Resources = sum .5 × people × log(1 + jointly net household change/baseline) / 1.03. Headline = 10 × cost/(clinical Q + resource equivalent).
model.counterfactual: Existing public violence prevention, employment and trauma services continue; alternative jobs, benefit offsets and funding replacement matter.
model.attribution: All population, risk, uptake, response, efficacy and resource success coefficients are conditional judgments, not recipient causal observations.
model.uncertainty: Complete portfolio and marginal-gift EV unknown; reference priors are not calibrated posterior estimates.
model.nativeOutcomes: Distinct local participants, avoided physical victimizations, finite trauma improvement and net household resources; no arrest-to-QALY conversion.
